reviews.author: Mike Rapoport
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Mike Rapoport suggested improving the patch description by adding a 'human touch' to make it more readable, but did not specify any technical issues or concrete suggestions.

Reviewer suggested reordering the patch series to place commits updating existing tests first, followed by new tests and infrastructure
reviews.raw_body:
My overall feeling is that changelogs need more human touch to be
parseable.

---

I'd put the commits that update the existing tests at the top of the
series and than add the new tests and infrastrucure.

-- 
Sincerely yours,
Mike.

reviews.author: Mike Rapoport
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Mike Rapoport suggested a minor improvement to the patch description, recommending that the word 'Virtual' be removed from the address field for better clarity.

Reviewer Mike Rapoport suggested that the patch description should not incrementally build upon the is_backed_by_folio() function, implying that it may be more accurate or clear to describe the new functionality independently.

Reviewer Mike Rapoport requested that the patch use 'VA' or simply 'address' instead of 'virtual address', as it's implied in a userspace context.
reviews.raw_body:
Nit:                          ^ address (even without Virtual) reads
better to me here and in the subject.

---

I don't think the description should be incremental on top of
is_backed_by_folio()

---

Please spell out VA or just use "address". selftests are userspace,
"virtual" is kinda implied.

-- 
Sincerely yours,
Mike.

reviews.author: Mike Rapoport
reviews.summary: Reviewer Mike Rapoport questioned whether the error message in khugepaged should include quotes, suggesting that opening /proc/self/pagemap would be sufficient.
reviews.raw_body:
Do we need quotes in perror() message?
open(/proc/self/pagemap) will do I think.

reviews.author: Mike Rapoport
reviews.summary: Reviewer Mike Rapoport suggested refactoring the existing code to run all supported configurations by default, similar to how the cow test works, and requested that a simple 'khugepaged' invocation should test everything it can before adding new options and tests.
reviews.raw_body:
Having options is usefull for targeted testing, but I think that the
default should be to run all supported confugrations, like e.g. cow test
does. That's the point of a selftest: check that everything works.

Can we refactor the existing code so that simple 'khugepaged' invocation
will test everything it can before adding new options and tests?

-- 
Sincerely yours,
Mike.

reviews.author: Mike Rapoport
reviews.summary: Reviewer Mike Rapoport noted that the khugepaged_full_pass() helper function is being used by other patches, and suggested that it should be introduced in a separate patch before its users.
reviews.raw_body:
This implies that _full_pass() helper should be in a patch before its
users :)

-- 
Sincerely yours,
Mike.

reviews.author: Mike Rapoport
reviews.summary: Reviewer Mike Rapoport requested that the default duration be set to 5 seconds for each mode and that ./khugepaged_race run all modes by default.
reviews.raw_body:
Please set the default duration so it will be 5 seconds for each mode
and make ./khugepaged_race run all the modes by default.

-- 
Sincerely yours,
Mike.

2026-08-03.patch_summary: This patch series improves the coverage of selftests for khugepaged, a mechanism that collapses huge pages in memory. The patches add new tests and helpers to ensure that khugepaged works correctly across various scenarios, including different page orders, collapse cases, and racing conditions. The changes also include improvements to existing tests and documentation. The goal is to provide a more comprehensive suite of selftests for khugepaged before its underlying mechanism is modified. The patches have been tested on x86-64 and arm64 architectures with 4K and 64K pages, respectively.

reviews.author: Kiryl Shutsemau (author)
reviews.summary: The author addressed Zi Yan's concern that non-uniform split of a pagecache folio could take over everywhere, explaining that uniform split still goes through xas_split_alloc() and that there are cases where a folio needs to be fully dissolved to order-0. The author does not think non-uniform split can simply take over everywhere.
reviews.raw_body:
Not really: xas_try_split() is the non-uniform path only.  A uniform split
of a pagecache folio still goes through xas_split_alloc(), in
__folio_split():

	if (split_type == SPLIT_TYPE_UNIFORM) {
		xas_set_order(&xas, folio->index, new_order);
		xas_split_alloc(&xas, folio, old_order, gfp);

and __split_unmapped_folio() keeps the two apart for a reason it states
itself:

	 * uniform split has xas_split_alloc() called before
	 * irq is disabled to allocate enough memory, whereas
	 * non-uniform split can handle ENOMEM.

So MAX_PAGECACHE_ORDER is still the limit.

I do not think non-uniform split can simply take over everywhere either.
There are going to be cases when a folio has to be fully dissolved to
order-0.

-- 
  Kiryl Shutsemau / Kirill A. Shutemov
